interventions.summary: A systematic review of randomized trials found most adults with lactose intolerance or malabsorption tolerate 12–15 g of lactose (about a cup of milk). Evidence for lactose-reduced milk, probiotics and other agents was insufficient.

generalEvidence.title: Systematic review: effective management strategies for lactose intolerance.

outcomes.quote: Evidence was insufficient that lactose-reduced solution or milk with a lactose content of 0 to 2 g, compared with greater than 12 g, is effective in reducing symptoms of lactose intolerance.

limitations: Most included trials studied malabsorption rather than symptoms.

population.value: Factor V Leiden heterozygotes and homozygotes
population.quote: Individuals who are heterozygous for the factor V Leiden variant have a slightly increased risk for VTE; individuals who are homozygous for the factor V Leiden variant have a much greater thrombotic risk.

Women with a history of VTE who are heterozygous for the factor V Leiden variant and women homozygous for the factor V Leiden variant with or without prior VTE should avoid estrogen-containing contraception and HRT.

limitations: Many people with the variant never develop a clot.
